The Quick, by Lauren Owen, is a tense read that kept me wanting to both find out what happens next and close the book and not look again.
The setting is Victorian England
not the pleasant BBC England we love on the tellie.
No, this is the England of Jack the Ripper and foggy streets and things that go bump in the night.
This England is dark and brooding and dangerous.
The characters are set in place slowly, and, at times, I was anxious for the author to just get on with it
the technique did add that tension I mentioned earlier, and allowed it to build.
The style of writing reminded me of 19th century authors, and I mean that in a positive way.
This really added to the Gothic flavor I felt the novel had.
Though there was no castle, per se, the whole of London lent itself as the creepy setting.
There is not romance in the traditional sense
there is a love story here, and heroes and heroines and good versus evil.

However, the author addresses the story elements with craft and style, and I definitely think that if you like suspense, the supernatural and horror with things that make you jump, and you like a novel that is also well written, then this is a new author to try.
